caption:
🩸🍬 Neonatal hypoglycaemia | PG Notes · Neonatology 07

🎯 Treat if blood glucose < 45 mg/dl (2.5 mmol/L), the operational threshold. Many babies are asymptomatic: screen the at-risk ones.

🔍 Screen: preterm · SGA/IUGR · LGA · infant of diabetic mother · sepsis · asphyxia · hypothermia · poor feeding

🩺 Symptoms: jitteriness, tremors · lethargy, poor feeding, weak cry · apnoea, cyanosis · hypotonia, hypothermia · seizures

🪜 Management:
1️⃣ Asymptomatic, mild: feed and recheck in 30–60 min
2️⃣ Symptomatic or persistent: 2 ml/kg of 10% dextrose IV
3️⃣ Then infusion at GIR 6–8 mg/kg/min
4️⃣ Still low: raise GIR in steps of 2 mg/kg/min
5️⃣ Refractory: think hyperinsulinism; hydrocortisone, glucagon, diazoxide

⭐ Pearls:
• GIR (mg/kg/min) = % dextrose × ml/kg/day ÷ 144
• Needing GIR > 8–10 suggests hyperinsulinism
• Commonest cause of persistent hypoglycaemia in infancy: congenital hyperinsulinism

📚 Ref: NNF clinical practice guidelines, AAP, Nelson
